theme: 3 terms on protocols: rules, new code and promises in Swift

terms.definition: A list of rules that says what properties and methods a type must have.
terms.example: Let's write a protocol, so every screen follows the same rules.

terms.definition: A way to add new methods to a type you already have, without editing its original code.
terms.example: I added a small extension to Int, so we can double any number.

terms.definition: When a type promises to follow a protocol by providing everything the protocol asks for.
terms.example: The compiler shows an error because Bird is missing its protocol conformance.

video.title: Protocol, Extension & Protocol Conformance in 2 minutes | iOS Daily English Day 9
video.description:
Learn to talk about protocols in Swift: Protocol, Extension and Protocol Conformance, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Protocol - A list of rules that says what properties and methods a type must have.
Extension - A way to add new methods to a type you already have, without editing its original code.
Protocol Conformance - When a type promises to follow a protocol by providing everything the protocol asks for.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

dialogue.title: Every pet makes a sound

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I want every pet to make a sound, but `Dog` and `Cat` share nothing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Write a protocol. A protocol lists what a type must be able to do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Then `Dog` needs protocol conformance, so it must add `sound()`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use an extension, so you don't edit the struct. Write `extension Dog: Pet`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wait, does an extension change the original `Dog`?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, it only adds a method to `Dog`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. A protocol for the rules, and the compiler checks protocol conformance.
Write a protocol, so every screen follows the same rules.
